paragraphs.source_en: Despite the variability of sites and shelters, their morphology does not seem to substantially affect the themes of paintings. In the Tassili, the characteristic elements are found in both open and hidden sites, suggesting that motifs important for this art were painted in all kinds of sites and shelters. For example, the same kind of masks, possibly representing stylized mouflon, are located in the open shelter at Tin Aboteka as well as in the hidden shelter at Uan Bender. On the Tassili Plateau the same symbols are located in different kinds of shelters, which means that the difference is not in the symbol but in the place. As for the Algerian Tadrart and the Acacus, the morphology of the shelters is generally open and the symbols common for this area also occur everywhere.
